title: Motocross rider control and course wear: current 100-image review

baselineAudit.policy: Original supplied metadata, URLs and prior observations remain in this existing audit. Per-image JSON pointers below resolve into it; its classifications are not promoted into current findings.

reviewMethods.root: All 100 originals visually reviewed on five labelled 20-image contact sheets. File hashes independently rechecked during this audit export.

interpretation: New means a reference principle guided a current change; it does not count one feature per image.
Retained and context are explicit current specialist decisions. Unclassified means sheet-reviewed without an individual specialist decision.
Images establish visual shape, attachment, soil structure and pose principles. Physics constants, subjective fun, source capture hardware and GPU performance are not measured from still images.

specialist.observation: Rocky forest shelf separates coarse mineral earth from grass and stratified rock.
specialist.application: Environmental scale reference; no mountain trail or ATV feature added.

specialist.observation: Low sunset light picks out fine beach sand and long vehicle shadows.
specialist.application: Sand-scale context; no beach, UTV or lighting change.

specialist.observation: The outside bank carries rough loose soil beside smoother, darker, separately ridden passages.
specialist.application: Extend independently wandering compacted passages across the authored corridor and retain loose shoulders.

specialist.observation: A close outdoor pack throws diffuse dust above reddish soil beside paddock canopies.
specialist.application: Retain loaded-wheel roost and existing event furniture.

specialist.observation: Lengthwise worn lines follow the forested jump section into the raised outside bank.
specialist.application: Prepared traffic follows the course frame and broadens through corners without changing jump geometry.

specialist.observation: Wide stadium start contains a packed field, red soil and rear-wheel debris.
specialist.application: Keep the actual start, course width and driven-wheel effects; no start-rule change.

specialist.observation: Tropical valley layers grassy islands, palms, dirt paths and distant coast.
specialist.application: Scale and composition context; no tropical venue.

specialist.observation: Granular desert trail has curved vehicle traces, outer stones and a soft rear plume.
specialist.application: Surface-scale context; no desert route or vehicle additions.

specialist.observation: Wooded trail contains deep cross bumps, ruts, yellow stakes and large boulders.
specialist.application: Retain authored physical chop and route geometry; the new skin does not add rideable bumps.

specialist.observation: Foreground mountain-course bumps have irregular tyre scoring and rougher soil between passages.
specialist.application: Broken pressure and centimetre torn-edge variation interrupt prepared traffic; loose clods have an uneven distribution.

specialist.observation: The stadium overview shows a locally reflective inside groove with much rougher surrounding soil.
specialist.application: Existing wet-film reservoir continues to follow grooves and terrain slope.

specialist.observation: A low rear view approaching the sporting arch shows coarse broken soil with nonuniform grain spacing.
specialist.application: Warp the fragment distribution so exposed loose soil no longer reads as a regular cell lattice.

specialist.observation: Freestyle compound is composed of graded banks, metal ramp frames and distinct landing structures.
specialist.application: No freestyle ramps or invented jump profiles.

specialist.observation: Broad graded banks and sharp faces carry worn swathes that vary across the dirt bowl.
specialist.application: Use authored half-width and independently interrupted pressure rather than five fixed central paths.

specialist.observation: The forest course shows many closely spaced, broken wheel and rake traces spanning the full visible dirt width.
specialist.application: More of the corridor carries compacted passages, with local merging and loose grass-edge shoulders.

specialist.observation: Open-roof stadium uses roof trusses, occupied tiers and block-bounded rhythm lanes.
specialist.application: Retain stadium structure and course furniture.

specialist.observation: Indoor rhythm lanes have pale packed lengthwise traces against rougher darker soil.
specialist.application: Separate broad compacted swathes, narrow cuts and raised loose lips at riding distance.

specialist.observation: Wide outdoor dirt lanes show numerous narrow grooves, differently sized jumps and pale dry edges.
specialist.application: Scale the prepared passage distribution to the authored width while fading to loose shoulders.

specialist.observation: Forest ATV scene separates pale compact grit, gray boulders and hard clods inside soft dust.
specialist.application: Mineral hierarchy context; existing ATV-independent roost is retained.

specialist.observation: A high outdoor bank shows a dark damp rut beside pale packed passing lines and granular loose earth.
specialist.application: Compacted swathes smooth the scanned normal while their cuts retain local relief and wet response.

specialist.observation: Low oblique stadium jump shows extended suspension and a nose-up bike against the stands.
specialist.application: Keep existing physical jump silhouette and bike presentation.

specialist.observation: A staggered pack crosses layered ruts with loose clods and rough granular soil between the lines.
specialist.application: Keep fragment distributions irregular between smoother compacted passages.

specialist.observation: Two airborne red motorcycles separate against trees and barriers with different chassis pitch.
specialist.application: Pose and composition context; no terrain change inferred from flight poses.

specialist.observation: Rear view up a crowded berm shows several distinct ridden lines from the inside to the bank.
specialist.application: Widen the visible prepared traffic family to offer readable course structure, without declaring an ideal line.

specialist.application: Keep existing exact terrain and suspension behavior; no static-pose inference added.

references.metadataDiscrepancyFromBaseline: The filename asserts a crash; the observed leaning/congested pose alone does not establish a fallen rider.

specialist.observation: Three crowded riders lean through a coarse berm with smoother worn troughs; the still alone does not establish a fallen rider.
specialist.application: Retain rough fragments outside smoother traffic cuts; no crash rule inferred from this image.

specialist.observation: A wide pack exits a berm toward a crest over pale granular dirt and distinct compacted passages.
specialist.application: Maintain traffic structure across both the broad lane and its narrowing jump approach.

specialist.observation: Congested outdoor corner uses warm translucent dust to separate overlapping riders.
specialist.application: Retain loaded-wheel dust/clod emission; no atmosphere subsystem added.

specialist.observation: A dark jump crest occludes riders beyond it and makes the foreground descending slope legible.
specialist.application: Keep the exact source mesh, ray intersections, jump shadow and camera clearance.

specialist.observation: Different upright/crouched riders accompany different airborne chassis attitudes. Transfer independent bounded body posture and bracing control; no torque or inertia is measured from the still.
A broad pack occupies separate lateral lines into a stadium corner. Preserve AI, gate and steering calibration.
Close pack shows deep forward crouch, supported boots, high elbows and loaded front ends. Manual fore/aft posture now shifts the loaded suspension with attachment kept by the existing rider pose.
Lean angles, upright torsos and inside-foot support remain readable together. Existing lateral lean and dab remain unchanged.
Rear chase view makes airborne opponents and the landing lane readable. Existing recoverable whips and camera remain unchanged.
A high jump leaves room to see the whole rider and future rhythm lanes. Existing ballistic trajectory remains independent of body controls.
Corner crop shows a defined rut, braced torso and inside boot. Existing rut and corner support remain calibrated.
Near upright rider and trailing airborne riders have distinct approach/landing poses. Independent rider posture supports those silhouette changes without an airborne path force.
Riders share a corner and connect directly to the next jumping lane. Existing collision and AI sequencing retained.
Promotional helmeted portraits and graphic typography do not provide physical control data.
Garage display provides rider/bike presentation context; no workshop feature added.
Packed launch ceremony and bright flame columns provide start composition; normal gate logic retained.
Broad starting pack with flags and flame trusses; normal acceleration and gate timing retained.
Three static rider portraits provide gear/brand presentation context, without dynamic evidence.

references.metadataDiscrepancyFromBaseline: The filename and visual_focus say two bikes; the image shows three motorcycles of different sizes.

specialist.observation: Garage shows multiple motorcycles and exposed mechanical negative space; no new garage interaction.
Wide colored arena light show supplies venue context, without new event lighting systems.
Separate experience tiers make assistance explicit. Sport/Raw semantics remain, with manual body control available to both.
The settings explicitly separate Air Control and Rider Weight from brakes. New independent riderLean control and root-owned UI/help explain effective finite body bracing alongside retained pedals.
A small central riding tip remains subordinate to the chase scene and distributed race HUD. Root integrates control help within existing interface.
Full side view shows standing knees, forward-supported torso and nose-down airborne chassis. Supports attached body pose range; reduced bracing-control sign is explicitly a game calibration.

references.metadataDiscrepancyFromBaseline: The filename says heavy roost; little airborne roost is visible. Coarse rutted soil is the useful observed evidence.

specialist.observation: Berm congestion includes leaning and contacting bikes across coarse grooves. Existing collision/recovery remains active.
Front starting pack and fire jets establish lighting hierarchy. Existing start logic retained.
Rear rider under flame arch is a lighting and silhouette reference; no new pyrotechnics.

references.metadataDiscrepancyFromBaseline: The filename mentions fire; no flames are visible in the supplied image.

specialist.observation: Airborne rider has a visibly composed supported body above an extended fork. Manual pose and finite bracing are independently controllable.
Rear contact traces a churned groove beneath a lifted front. Previously implemented per-wheel pickup remains; new grounded weight shift uses actual end loads.
Tropical ATV sunset is vehicle/setting context outside this motorcycle control change.
ATV corner shows material ejection at loaded tyre contact. Existing wheel-driven roost remains unchanged.
A rider braces above an extended front end while the rear follows the face. Independently shifting supported weight affects the actual suspension rather than adding jump boost.
Standing motorcycle rider above sharp ridges and a raised front shows rear-biased loading. Body control provides a bounded forward/back weighting choice.
Mixed ATV/motorcycle forest pack supplies venue/vehicle context; no new vehicle family.
Close ATV battle is outside the two-wheel body dynamics implementation.
UTV jump demonstrates another vehicle silhouette, without implying UTV physics changes.
Long chase view exposes repeated landing corridors. Existing landing targets and ballistic path remain, with manual body correction available during the same flight.
